title: In-Memory Key-Value Store with Transactions
description:
Implement an in-memory key-value store that supports nested transactions.

Your program reads commands from standard input, one per line, and prints output only for the commands that produce it. Keys and values are single words containing no spaces. Command names are uppercase.

Data commands:
  SET <key> <value>   Store value under key. Prints nothing.
  GET <key>           Print the current value for key, or NULL if it is not set.
  DELETE <key>        Remove key. Prints nothing.
  COUNT <value>       Print how many keys currently hold exactly this value.

Transaction commands:
  BEGIN               Open a new transaction. Transactions may be nested.
  ROLLBACK            Undo every change made since the most recent BEGIN and
                      close that transaction. If no transaction is open,
                      print NO TRANSACTION.
  COMMIT              Permanently apply the changes from ALL open transactions
                      and close them. If no transaction is open, print
                      NO TRANSACTION.
  END                 Stop reading input and exit.

Rules:
  - Changes made inside an open transaction are visible to GET and COUNT
    immediately, but only become permanent when COMMIT runs.
  - ROLLBACK undoes only the innermost open transaction. Any enclosing
    transaction stays open, and the changes it made before the inner BEGIN
    remain in effect.
  - COMMIT closes every open transaction at once, not just the innermost one.
  - COUNT must reflect the current state, including uncommitted changes, and
    must never count a key that has been deleted.
  - A key that was never set, or that has been deleted, reads as NULL.

Input Format:
  A sequence of commands, one per line, terminated by END.

Output Format:
  One line for each GET, each COUNT, and each NO TRANSACTION error, in the
  order the commands appear.

Example:
  Input:
    SET a hello
    GET a
    BEGIN
    SET a world
    GET a
    ROLLBACK
    GET a
    ROLLBACK
    END
  Output:
    hello
    world
    hello
    NO TRANSACTION
